title: Anthony Mary Claret (24 October)
hookLine: a weaver turned archbishop of Cuba and founder of the Claretians

cards: A loom is a loud machine. The shuttle flies back and forth, the frame knocks, and one slip shows in the cloth for good. In Catalonia, in Spain, a young man from a weaving family went to work at the looms in Barcelona.

He was good at it, good enough that the work filled his head. Years later that same man would be an archbishop across the ocean, in Cuba, and the founder of a family of missionaries who still carry his name.
He kept weaving, just with different thread.

teach.b: Anthony Mary Claret wrote an account of his own life, and he's honest in it. As a young weaver, he says, even at Mass his mind was full of looms and patterns, more machinery than prayer.

teach.h: A LINE FROM THE GOSPEL CAUGHT HIM.
teach.b: Then, his account says, a line from the Gospel caught him and wouldn't let go: what does it profit a man to gain the whole world and lose his own soul? He left the looms and became a priest.
What came next looks like weaving on a larger frame. He walked from town to town in Catalonia preaching, and wrote small, cheap books and pamphlets so people could take something home.
He gathered other priests into a missionary community, the Missionary Sons of the Immaculate Heart of Mary, known today as the Claretians.

Then he was sent to Cuba as archbishop of Santiago. He kept going on foot and on horseback, visiting parishes, and he spoke against the cruelty done to enslaved people and the poor. That made enemies.
His own account tells of a man who attacked him with a knife and wounded him in the face, and of Claret asking that the man be spared.

teach.h: THE CHARITY OF CHRIST PRESSETH US.
teach.b: His motto was a line of Paul: "For the charity of Christ presseth us." The love of Christ pushes, urges, won't let you sit still.
A weaver carries every thread all the way across and ties it off, and Claret seems to have lived that way.

how: Catholics keep the memorial of Saint Anthony Mary Claret on 24 October, and the Claretian missionaries he founded keep it as their founder's day.

games.q: you're a young weaver, good at the work, and a line from the Gospel won't leave you alone. what do you do?
o: leave the looms and become a priest.
weave altar cloths for the church.
games.why: Claret left the looms for the priesthood, and spent the rest of his life preaching, writing and founding.

practice: Pick something small that's been left half done, a drawer, a reply, a dish in the sink, and give it a weaver's attention now, right down to the last little part you usually skip: the wiping down, the final check, the knot at the end.
If you pray, offer the finished thing to God; if not, simply notice what it's like to see one small thing through.
